answer: An identity that can be stamped out like a cheap opal on a stall is not scarce enough to trust. The useful filter is a bridge that only opens after work and locked stake have already been spent, so a new name cannot walk across just by arriving. A cipher here is not a riddle; it is a record that will not decrypt for a swarm of aliases unless each one can show the same costly history, which a factory of wallets cannot mint as fast as it can copy a face.
